query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of silicon (Si) into face-centered-cubic (FCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) will improve their dynamic strength-ductility performance.
generation.intervention: Introduction of silicon (Si) into the alloy
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced stacking fault energy (SFE) of the matrix
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening effect and induction of more deformation mechanisms to enhance plasticity
generation.boundary: Applicable to FCC HEAs under dynamic loading conditions
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Si introduction and the specific dynamic loading conditions under which the improvement occurs are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the dynamic strength-ductility performance of Si-introduced FCC HEAs with untreated FCC HEAs under controlled dynamic loading conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Si-introduced FCC HEAs do not exhibit improved dynamic strength-ductility performance compared to the untreated FCC HEAs, the hypothesis is falsified

Paper node: Enhanced strength–ductility synergy in ultrafine-grained eutectic high-entropy alloys by inheriting microstructural lamellae (2019). Cited 2 times before the cutoff; 1 papers in this graph say something specific about it.
What citing papers say about it:
- cites (from "Simultaneously enhancing the ultimate strength and ductility of ...", 2021): A soft FCC lamella matrix with a hard intergranular B2 (an ordered BCC) phase was designed in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA for the simultaneous strength-ductility enhancement.

Paper node: Synergetic effect of Si addition on mechanical properties in face-centered-cubic high entropy alloys: a first-principles study (2022). Cited 1 times before the cutoff; 1 papers in this graph say something specific about it.
What citing papers say about it:
- cites (from "Effect of Si on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties ...", 2023): Previous studies reported that Si doping in the MEAs/HEAs can improve the strength and ductility synergistically by reducing the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the matrix .
- cites (from "Effect of Si on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties ...", 2023): This synergistic improvement of strength and ductility is mainly due to the fact that the dissolved Si atoms in the matrix can not only reduce the SFE of the MEA matrix , helping to induce more deformation mechanisms to enhance plasticity but also improve the strength of the MEA by causing a significant solid solution strengthening effect .
